about: The one table of what a model call costs: the runtime prices messages from it, the evaluation script prints its cost column from it, and a bundle test checks every model price in a bundle price list against it. US dollars per million tokens. A line holds from this file's date until a later file has a line for the same provider and model. Never edited after it is committed (a test pins its bytes): a changed price is a new file with a new date. A model in no line is UNKNOWN, never free. 'provider' is the name runtime.json gives the model, for example deepinfra.

inrPerUsd.note: Rupees to the dollar, as the runtime has always used it, so no stored cost changes. The economics note says 88 (and the proposed bundle price list follows it); its examples come out the same at 87 or 88. The owner decides, in a new dated file.

rates.note: Runs on the shop server's own CPU (section 3.2): no price per call. Zero here means no per-call charge, not an unknown price.
About $0.042 per million tokens, as the Laya page quotes it (section 3.2); a 1,500 token request is about INR 0.0055. Confirm on the first invoice.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, DeepInfra Flex tier (section 3.2, third-party trackers; Standard is $0.20 / $0.60). Check deepinfra.com. Any id naming DeepSeek V4.1 Flash matches, because DeepInfra's exact id is not confirmed.
Prompts up to 100,000 tokens; cache reads ($0.01) not used. Reasoning is billed as output, so real usage can be higher. As in the bundle lists of 3 and 4 Nov.
Paid tier only (the free tier's text is used for training, which WhatsApp's terms forbid). The page has no date. As in the bundle lists of 3 and 4 Nov.
